issues.message: alive() treats a pid as dead whenever `ps -o lstart=` returns nothing (ps missing, restricted container, ps error), because `now is not None` is required. holder_alive() then reports a live holder as provably dead, and the queue head reclaims the lock (remove()) while the command still runs; tickets() also prunes live waiters' tickets. Two runs then hold the same mutex (e.g. two Gradle/disk-heavy builds), defeating the safeguard.
issues.fix: Distinguish 'pid absent' (os.kill ESRCH) from 'ps failed'. If os.kill succeeds and ps yields nothing, return True (unknown = alive) and never auto-reclaim or prune on that basis.

issues.message: commit_plan stages and commits every changed or untracked file matching a track glob, with no protected-path or secret filter. A broad glob (`**`, `src/**`) lets an untracked non-ignored `.env`, CI, Docker or Terraform file be committed by `team commit --yes`. The built-in rule only tells the executor not to touch them; the orchestrator's commit path does not enforce it.
issues.fix: In commit_plan, refuse (or move to foreign) paths matching .env*, .github/**, .gitlab-ci*, Dockerfile*, k8s/terraform dirs, *.pem, *.key, unless an explicit --allow-protected PATH is given.

issues.message: Checkpoint tars every untracked non-ignored file, including stray secrets (.env.local, keys), into <bank>/backups/team/*-untracked.tar.gz with default umask permissions. The dir lives in the bank and the script only warns when it is already tracked, so it can be committed or shared. The manifest also lists their paths.
issues.fix: umask 077 and mkdir -m 700 for --dir; skip a secret-name denylist (same as SEC-2) and record it in skipped_large; ensure the dir is gitignored.

issues.message: $topic is never validated in the script (only --label is) and goes into cid, which is used as a file path: `--topic ../../x` writes the diff/tar/manifest outside --dir. The Python caller needs an existing reports/<topic>/team.json, which limits reachability, but direct script use and mb_team_state.find_topic accept an unvalidated --topic (team_file joins it unchecked).
issues.fix: Validate topic with TOPIC_RE (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$) in the script and in find_topic. Validate the verify <id> the same way.

issues.message: verify trusts file names in the .sha256 file: `os.path.join(out, name)` with an absolute or `..` name hashes an arbitrary file. The impact is limited (a mismatch is reported, no content disclosed), but a tampered sha file makes verify an oracle and also proves nothing about integrity, since the manifest and sha file sit in the same writable dir.
issues.fix: Require name == os.path.basename(name) and a cid-prefix match; ignore other lines.

issues.message: checkpoint.extra, resource maintenance and precondition `check` run via shell (`bash -c`/shell=True) from pipeline.yaml. They are trusted project config, but a cloned repo's .memory-bank/pipeline.yaml runs arbitrary commands on `team checkpoint` and on every `mb-lock run`, with no confirmation or display before the first run.
issues.fix: Document the trust boundary in commands/team.md; print the command before running; optionally require a one-time confirm or hash pin for project-level (not bundled) commands.

issues.message: `--rev` is unvalidated and is rendered unquoted into a backticked copy-paste command (`git diff <prev> <rev>`) and prompt.md. A rev containing a shell separator followed by a second command becomes a ready-to-run line for the external reviewer. Likewise mb_team_tracks.py:153 prints `mb_contract.py freeze {contract} --tree {tree}` without shlex.quote, as does the `tree` slot in track-prompt.md.
issues.fix: Validate rev against ^[0-9A-Za-z._/~^-]+$ (or run `rev-parse --verify`), and shlex.quote contract/tree/skill in every rendered command.

issues.message: BREACH=$(mktemp) && rm -f is followed by a later `: >"$BREACH"`, so the marker is created at a known name in TMPDIR after removal (a TOCTOU window; a pre-planted symlink or file fakes or breaks the stop signal). Practical risk is low because the name is random.
issues.fix: Use a private dir (mktemp -d) and a marker file inside it, or have the watcher write the marker with set -o noclobber.

issues.message: break --reason is free text posted verbatim to the board STATUS entry, so a pasted secret ends up in the shared board.
issues.fix: Truncate the reason to 200 characters and note in the docs that it is public to the team.

summary: No blockers. Confirmed correct: eval of `py env` is shlex-quoted; the lock root is 0700 and rejects a symlink or foreign owner, never uses TMPDIR; the commit path uses --literal-pathspecs and --only on explicit files, with no push; bank is shlex.quoted in rendered commands; track ids, topic (init) and external --name are regex-validated; the run board entry carries only the program name. Main risks: stale-lock reclaim on a ps failure (SEC-1), no protected-path/secret guard on commit or checkpoint (SEC-2/3), and unvalidated topic/rev/verify id at the edges (SEC-4/5/7). Counts: blocker 0, major 0, medium 3, minor 4, nit 2.
